The challenge

You want AI in your product and in how you build it. The safe path is not obvious.

AI can draft code in hours. Someone still has to own the architecture, the security review, and the release.

Agents need access to systems that were never built for them. Legacy systems, GDPR, budgets, and unclear ownership slow every decision, for good reasons.

Carrying those questions while the roadmap keeps moving is hard.

We believe AI should make your senior engineers faster. It should not replace their judgment.

That is agentic engineering, not vibe coding.

Already have an AI-built app? Take the 12-question readiness check.

Your path

Three steps to a first release

  1. 1 Talk it through One call to map your situation, constraints, and goals.
  2. 2 Prove it small A prototype or Lighthouse Project: one journey, a small blast radius, a reviewable first step.
  3. 3 Build it with your team We deliver alongside you and hand over the specifications, tests, and release gates.

You keep the codebase, the decisions, and the practices. No lock-in.

Ready for step 1? Start a Project. Want the detail? See our full process.

Why now

AI moves at warp speed. Your first step should not wait.

AI tools change in months, not years. The company-wide plan will take time, for good reasons. Your first step does not have to.

Without shared review rules, a missed issue can turn into rework just before a release. In many teams, AI-written code already arrives here and there, faster than anyone can review it. That builds pressure between the people who build and the people who sign off.

Speed has a second cost. When building outruns feedback, the customer voice may get quieter. Teams can ship more and learn less.

The rules do not wait either. If your customers talk to an AI your company offers, you usually have to tell them so. The EU AI Act (opens in a new tab) has required this since 2 August 2026.

So why not pick one thing that can make a real difference in a few weeks? Start with a small team and one project. See how it works in practice, and how it resonates across your organization.

Before and after

What changes for your team

The goal: your team ships with AI on a steady rhythm. Here is the change we work toward with you.

  • Before AI writes code faster than your team can review it.

    After Your engineers review each change against agreed tests and review rules.

  • Before Agent access waits on legal, security, and data questions, for good reasons.

    After Approved AI agents, from ChatGPT to Siri, can take a few defined product actions, such as checking an order. Actions require consent and leave an audit trail.

  • Before Releases go out faster than feedback comes in.

    After Customer feedback and analytics flow back into the product after each release. AI can help collect and sort them, so the loop is not forgotten.

  • Before The company-wide AI plan is still taking shape.

    After One Lighthouse Project gives that plan real evidence.

  • Before AI-written code and AI features make releases harder to predict.

    After Each release goes through the same tests, AI evals (repeatable checks of what the AI says and does), and release gates.

What that can look like: a working AI prototype for a ~3M-customer operator app. One senior engineer, AI-assisted, built it in four days as an internal sprint. A prototype, not a production launch. See the operator case in our work.

A working product. A team that can keep moving it.
